provenance: Constructed English-only teaching cases; not recordings, real machine output, or a translation benchmark.

cases.label: Negation lost before translation
cases.spoken: The meeting is not on Friday.
cases.observable_failure: The source transcript removes not and reverses the announcement.
cases.next_action: Check intelligible source audio and correct the transcript or use the available correction channel.
cases.pass_recheck: The reviewed transcript and the recipient's corrected information both retain the negative statement.

cases.label: Number substitution
cases.spoken: The group meets at six fifteen.
cases.source_transcript: The group meets at six fifty.
cases.observable_failure: The transcript changes the announced time.
cases.next_action: Check the announced time with the service team and replay the phrase using the actual input.
cases.pass_recheck: The transcript and corrected receiving-side message identify six fifteen.

cases.label: Room name becomes an ordinary phrase
cases.spoken: Meet in River Hall after the service.
cases.source_transcript: Meet in river haul after the service.
cases.observable_failure: The fictional room name is no longer identifiable in the transcript.
cases.next_action: Confirm spelling with the source owner and test the complete phrase; a vocabulary hint is optional only if the tool supports it.
cases.pass_recheck: The received information points unambiguously to the intended room.

cases.label: Book name changed
cases.spoken: The reading is from John chapter three.
cases.source_transcript: The reading is from Job chapter three.
cases.observable_failure: The transcript names a different book; no Scripture text is supplied.
cases.next_action: Compare the spoken reference with the speaker's checked outline and correct the book name.
cases.pass_recheck: Book and chapter identify the speaker's intended reference in both the transcript and the receiving-side correction.

cases.label: Condition changed
cases.spoken: If the hall is closed, wait by the entrance.
cases.source_transcript: The hall is closed. Wait by the entrance.
cases.observable_failure: A conditional instruction is presented as a fact.
cases.next_action: Review the whole sentence, not just the nouns, then communicate the corrected condition.
cases.pass_recheck: The listener can distinguish what to do if the hall is closed from whether it is currently closed.

cases.label: Unexplained theological term
cases.observable_failure: No target wording or explanation of the intended use is available; translation correctness cannot be judged.
cases.next_action: Ask the speaker for the intended sense and let a competent language reviewer consider the sentence in context.
cases.pass_recheck: The intended use, proposed wording, reviewer, and review reasoning are recorded; no definition is invented by this kit.

cases.label: Idiom needs the speaker's meaning
cases.spoken: We are on the same page.
cases.source_transcript: We are on the same page.
cases.observable_failure: The English phrase could concern a physical page or an idiom; no target output is available to assess.
cases.next_action: Ask what the speaker means in the surrounding passage and review an explanation or rendering with the language reviewer.
cases.pass_recheck: The reviewer can explain how the received wording preserves the speaker's stated meaning.

cases.label: Only a target-language complaint is available
cases.observable_failure: A listener reports a confusing sentence, but no source audio, transcript, or target wording has been retained.
cases.next_action: Record what can be established without inventing the missing sentence; arrange a permitted reproduction with the speaker and reviewer.
cases.pass_recheck: A new observed sample provides enough evidence to classify the problem; the original incident remains unclassified.

cases.label: Quotation boundary disappears
cases.spoken: Maya asked, 'Is the hall open?' I answered, 'Not yet.'
cases.source_transcript: Maya asked is the hall open I answered not yet.
cases.observable_failure: The words are present, but the display does not clearly distinguish the reported question from the answer.
cases.next_action: Review punctuation and attribution cues in the format recipients actually receive; Maya is a fictional name.
cases.pass_recheck: A reviewer can identify who asked the question and who answered without relying on the original audio.

cases.label: A paraphrase is mislabeled as a quotation
cases.spoken: I will summarize the point in my own words.
cases.source_transcript: I will summarize the point in my own words.
cases.observable_failure: A hypothetical display labels the following material an exact quotation even though the speaker identifies a summary.
cases.next_action: Remove the unsupported exact-quotation label and check the chosen source/version only when an actual quotation is intended.
cases.pass_recheck: The displayed attribution distinguishes a summary from quoted source text.

cases.label: Minor punctuation with meaning preserved
cases.observable_failure: A comma is absent. In this constructed source-language example the intended thanks remains clear.
cases.next_action: Ask the reviewer whether punctuation affects meaning or readability in the actual context before assigning severity.
cases.pass_recheck: Reviewer confirms meaning and readability remain usable; do not infer target-language accuracy from this example.

cases.label: Transcript correct, target review still required
cases.spoken: Please wait outside until the hall opens.
cases.source_transcript: Please wait outside until the hall opens.
cases.observable_failure: The source transcript is correct, but no actual translated wording or competent target-language assessment exists.
cases.next_action: Obtain the actual target output and an independent language review. Do not fabricate a bad translation for this exercise.
cases.pass_recheck: A reviewer checks location and waiting condition against the intended message; only observed target evidence can support a TRANSLATION diagnosis.
